Its offerings include personal loans, the Upgrade Card and OneCard credit cards that convert purchases into fixed-rate installment plans, home improvement and auto financing, buy-now-pay-later travel financing through Uplift, which it acquired in 2023 for US$100 million, high-yield savings and rewards checking accounts, and free credit monitoring tools. Loans and cards are issued through partner banks, and Upgrade earns revenue mainly from interest, origination fees and the sale of loans to institutional investors. It has helped customers access more than US$50 billion of consumer credit since it began lending in 2017, and its annualised revenue passed US$1 billion in May 2025. The company is headquartered in San Francisco, with an operations center in Phoenix, Arizona, a technology center in Montreal and about 1,950 employees. It was founded in 2016 by Renaud Laplanche, the co-founder and former chief executive of LendingClub. Upgrade has raised about US$750 million of equity from investors including Union Square Ventures, Ribbit Capital, Koch Disruptive Technologies, Coatue, DST Global and Neuberger Berman, most recently at a US$7.3 billion valuation in October 2025.

BharatPe
BharatPe is a Delhi-headquartered fintech company enabling digital payments for small merchants via UPI QR codes and POS terminals across India. The platform provides business loans, vendor financing, and soundbox devices for transaction confirmations, partnering with banks like Axis and Unity Small Finance Bank.

Krungthai Card
Krungthai Card PCL engaged in credit cards, personal loans and other related businesses. The Company provides services such as Credit Cards, Personal Loans, KTC Brother Boom Money, MAAI by KTC, Shop business and many. The company operations relate to a single business segment which is the financial services business and are carried out in a single geographic area which is Thailand.

Cross River Bank
Cross River Bank is a technology-focused regulated bank and financial-infrastructure provider. Its products combine software, operations and support needed to deliver the service reliably in its target market. The company serves fintech platforms, payment companies, lenders and businesses embedding banking products, and its offering addresses a repeatable commercial or operational workflow rather than an unrelated namesake activity. It earns interest income, origination, payments, banking-as-a-service and platform fees, which explains how customers pay and how the company sustains the product. Public company material and transaction reporting establish that the bank acquired HUBUC in July 2024 to expand embedded-finance capabilities. Those sources also anchor the website, location, founding year and ownership identity used in this correction. This expanded profile records the business model, customer group, revenue mechanism and relevant transaction history required for participant-level deal validation.

Grab Financial Group
Grab Financial Group is the financial services arm of the Southeast Asian super app Grab, launched in 2018. It offers digital payments, consumer and merchant lending, insurance and wealth products to the users, driver-partners and merchants of the Grab ecosystem. The unit aims to give underbanked consumers and small businesses simple and affordable financial products across Southeast Asia. In January 2021 it raised more than 300 million US dollars in a Series A round led by Hanwha Asset Management at a reported valuation of 3 billion US dollars. The parent company, Grab Holdings, is listed in the United States and reports financial services as one of its operating segments.

OnePay
OnePay is a financial mobile app providing banking, fintech solutions, online payments, cash transactions, and digital wallet services based in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The app supports transfers, bill payments, and QR code scanning for merchants. OnePay serves consumers and businesses in Southeast Asia with integrated financial tools.

Kakao Pay
kakaopay Corp is a mobile payment and digital wallet service provider. It provides easy payment, easy remittance, and other financial services. It operates in two segments: Financial Services and Non-financial Services.

Ualá
Ualá is an Argentine financial technology company that runs a digital banking platform for consumers and merchants across Argentina, Mexico and Colombia. It was founded in 2017 by Pierpaolo Barbieri and started with a mobile app linked to a prepaid Mastercard card. The app now offers debit and credit cards, transfers, bill payments, loans, investment funds, insurance and a remunerated account, while its merchant arm Ualá Bis provides card acceptance. Ualá bought the digital bank Wilobank in Argentina, the Mexican bank ABC Capital, the buy-now-pay-later lender Ceibo Creditos and the e-commerce platform Empretienda. It became a unicorn in August 2021 with a USD 350 million Series D and was valued at USD 3.2 billion after a USD 195 million round in March 2026. The company serves more than 11 million customers.

Capri Global Capital
Capri Global Capital Ltd provides financial services. The company is engaged in providing loans to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), providing long term finance for the construction of residential houses, retail lending, gold loan, and ancillary services. It generates maximum revenue from the interest income. Geographically, it operates only in India.

Uzum
Uzum is a Tashkent-headquartered super-app ecosystem powering e-commerce and fintech in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. It encompasses Uzum Market for online retail, Uzum Bank for digital payments and loans, Uzum Delivery for logistics, and services like utility bill payments and ride-hailing. The platform integrates shopping, finance, and everyday utilities into one interface. Businesses leverage its marketplace to access millions of consumers across Central Asia.

Creditas
Creditas is a Brazilian financial technology company that offers loans secured by homes, cars and payroll, together with insurance and a used-car marketplace. It was founded in 2012 by Sergio Furio as BankFacil and renamed Creditas in 2017. The company funds its loans largely through securitisation vehicles and, since the closing of its purchase of Bank Andbank Brasil in late 2025, holds a banking licence. Its Series G round of USD 108 million in December 2025 was led by Andbank at a post-money valuation of USD 3.3 billion, down from USD 4.8 billion in 2022. Earlier backers include SoftBank, Fidelity, Kaszek, QED Investors, VEF, Lightrock and Amadeus Capital. Acquisitions include Creditoo, Bcredi, Minuto Seguros, Volanty and Kzas, and it holds an investment in the electric motorcycle maker Voltz.

Greenlight
Greenlight is a financial technology company offering a debit card and app for family money management. The platform enables parents to set spending limits, assign chores with automated allowances, and facilitate investments in stocks and ETFs for children. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and launched in 2014, Greenlight partners with Visa for its Level 1 debit cards and provides cash back rewards up to 3 percent on purchases. The service covers earning, saving, spending, gifting, and investing features tailored for parents and kids across the United States.

Valiant Holding
Valiant Holding AG is an independent retail and SME bank which offers banking and financial services to clients. The company operates exclusively within Switzerland. The products and services of the company encompass mobile banking app and payment solution Twint, savings account, retirement planning solutions, payments, investing, financing products and advisory services, and customized investment solutions.
